section: States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali) and the States Reorganisation Act 1956
subsections: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: According to the States Reorganisation Commission, under what condition could Telangana merge with Andhra after the 1961 general elections?
o: Approval by a two-thirds majority of the Telangana Legislature
Approval by the Hyderabad State High Court
Approval by a simple majority of the Andhra Legislature
Approval by the Union Parliament through a constitutional amendment
accepted.x: The SRC recommended that Telangana remain separate initially, with a possible merger after the 1961 elections if the Telangana Legislature approved it by a two-thirds majority.
accepted.tq: Test the exact condition attached to a deferred merger.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: Who described the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism” in October 1953?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru referred to the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism” in October 1953.
accepted.tq: Match the political remark with its speaker and time.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission recommended, for the time being, that Hyderabad State should remain separate with which city as its capital?
accepted.x: The SRC recommended keeping Hyderabad State, comprising Telangana, separate temporarily, with Hyderabad as its capital.
accepted.tq: Use the location-based distinction between the proposed separate state and its capital.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gentlemen’s Agreement of 1956:
1. It provided for a Telangana Regional Council.
2. It provided that Telangana’s surplus revenues should be spent in Telangana.
3. It retained the Mulki rules.
4. It stipulated that the Deputy Chief Minister should belong to the other region when the Chief Minister belonged to one region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe safeguards agreed upon by the Andhra and Telangana leaders under the Gentlemen’s Agreement.
accepted.tq: Check each safeguard separately before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: The Gentlemen’s Agreement between the leaders of Andhra and Telangana was concluded on:
accepted.x: The Gentlemen’s Agreement was concluded on 20 February 1956 at Hyderabad House in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced dates in the reorganisation process.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Andhra Pradesh was formed
B. The Chief Ministers of Andhra and Hyderabad agreed to merge
C. Nehru described the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism”
D. The Gentlemen’s Agreement was concluded
accepted.x: The correct sequence is October 1953, 22 October 1955, 20 February 1956 and 1 November 1956.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate agreements.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: The agreement of 22 October 1955 between the Chief Ministers of Andhra and Hyderabad was reached at:
accepted.x: The Chief Ministers of Andhra and Hyderabad agreed to merge at Hyderabad House, New Delhi, on 22 October 1955.
accepted.tq: Test the exact venue attached to a major political agreement.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Congress sub-committee of November 1955 is correct?
o: It consisted of Nehru, Maulana Azad and G.B. Pant.
It unanimously rejected the merger of Andhra and Telangana.
It was chaired by the Chief Minister of Hyderabad.
It consisted of Patel, Rajendra Prasad and B.R. Ambedkar.
accepted.x: The Congress sub-committee comprised Jawaharlal Nehru, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and G.B. Pant. Azad continued to oppose the merger, while Nehru was greeted with Visalandhra slogans in Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Use the membership of the committee to reject swapped-person distractors.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh formed on 1 November 1956?
accepted.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy became the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh after its formation on 1 November 1956.
accepted.tq: Apply the office-holder trap by distinguishing leaders associated with the pre-merger states.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s:
With reference to the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956, consider the following statements:
1. Hyderabad was made its capital.
2. The merger followed the Gentlemen’s Agreement.
3. The SRC had originally recommended immediate merger without conditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Hyderabad became the capital and the merger followed the safeguards of the Gentlemen’s Agreement. The SRC had initially recommended keeping Telangana separate, not immediate unconditional merger.
accepted.tq: Identify the single reversed recommendation in an otherwise correct sequence.
accepted.sec: SRC on Visalandhra - conditions and time-frame

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 provided for the establishment of Zonal Councils under which Part of the Act?
accepted.x: The Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
accepted.tq: Test the exact statutory location rather than the broad subject of the Act.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five Zonal Councils established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
accepted.x: The five councils are Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern. The North-Eastern Council was created separately under the North-Eastern Council Act, 1971.
accepted.tq: Find the body created under a separate law rather than under the 1956 Act.

accepted.s: Who is the Chairman of each of the five Zonal Councils?
o: The senior-most Chief Minister in the zone
accepted.x: The Union Home Minister serves as the Chairman of all five Zonal Councils.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-role distinction to avoid confusing the Chairman with the Vice-Chairman.

accepted.s: The Vice-Chairman of a Zonal Council is selected from among the Chief Ministers of its member States by:
o: Nomination by the Union Home Minister for a five-year term
accepted.x: The Chief Ministers of member States serve as Vice-Chairman by annual rotation.
accepted.tq: Test the tenure and rotation rule attached to a constitutional-style office.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of Zonal Councils:
1. Each member State sends its Chief Minister and two Ministers.
2. Administrators or Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories are included.
3. Advisers such as Chief Secretaries have voting rights in the Councils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Each State is represented by its Chief Minister and two Ministers, and Administrators or Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories are included. Advisers such as Chief Secretaries attend without voting rights.
accepted.tq: Separate the composition of members from the non-voting status of advisers.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the role assigned in the Zonal Councils?
o: Union Home Minister — annual rotating Vice-Chairman
accepted.x: Development Commissioners are among the advisers who participate without voting rights. The Union Home Minister is Chairman, while State Chief Ministers rotate as Vice-Chairman.
accepted.tq: Distinguish advisers without vote from statutory members and office-bearers.

accepted.s: The Secretariat of the Zonal Councils is provided by the:
accepted.x: The Inter-State Council Secretariat serves as the Secretariat of the Zonal Councils.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative support body rather than the policy ministry.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of the Zonal Councils?
o: They are judicial bodies whose decisions are binding on States.
They are statutory, deliberative and advisory bodies whose recommendations are not binding.
They are executive bodies that directly allocate State finances.
They are constitutional bodies with powers to dissolve State Legislatures.
accepted.x: Zonal Councils are statutory, deliberative and advisory bodies. Their recommendations are not binding on the States.
accepted.tq: Match the institution’s actual function with the level of legal authority it possesses.

accepted.s: The North-Eastern Council was established under the:
accepted.x: The North-Eastern Council is a separate body established under the North-Eastern Council Act, 1971, unlike the five Zonal Councils created under the 1956 Act.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named regional bodies and their enabling laws.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh is included in the:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is a member of the Southern Zonal Council.
accepted.tq: Test State-to-zone membership directly.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT treated by the States Reorganisation Commission as a factor in reorganising States?
accepted.x: The SRC considered administrative efficiency, economic and financial viability, geographical contiguity, national unity and security, and the welfare of people and the national plan. Uniformity of political party representation was not listed as a principle.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated criterion among the recognised reorganisation principles.

accepted.s: Which approach best describes the States Reorganisation Commission’s treatment of linguistic homogeneity?
o: It recommended that every linguistic group be placed in one Union Territory.
It treated linguistic homogeneity as important but not the sole factor.
It accepted the principle of one language, one State without exception.
accepted.x: The SRC rejected the rigid formula of “one language, one State”. Linguistic homogeneity was considered a major factor, but it was balanced against other national and administrative considerations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a qualified principle from an absolute slogan.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the principles of State reorganisation:
1. Preservation of national unity and security was considered.
2. Welfare of the people and the national plan were considered.
3. Linguistic homogeneity was treated as the only relevant factor.
4. Geographical contiguity was considered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: National unity and security, people’s welfare and the national plan, and geographical contiguity were among the factors considered. Linguistic homogeneity was not treated as the only factor.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the listed administrative and national criteria.

accepted.s: The States Reorganisation Commission’s recommendation to examine the reorganisation of States “holistically” implies consideration of:
o: A combination of linguistic, administrative, economic, geographical and national factors
Only the wishes of the existing State governments
Only the financial position of a proposed State
accepted.x: A holistic approach required balancing linguistic considerations with administrative efficiency, economic viability, geographical contiguity, national unity and public welfare.
accepted.tq: Translate a broad principle into its practical combination of factors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly illustrates the SRC’s rejection of the idea that every language should have only one State?
o: It prohibited the formation of all linguistic States.
It made language irrelevant in every case.
It converted all linguistic regions into Union Territories.
It divided same-language areas into more than one State where other factors warranted it.
accepted.x: The SRC was not solely a Linguistic States Commission; it could divide areas sharing a language into more than one State when other considerations required it.
accepted.tq: Use the example-based interpretation of a general principle.

accepted.s: Bombay State was bifurcated into Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960 mainly following the:
o: Akali Dal and Punjabi Suba movements
accepted.x: The Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat movements led to the division of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.
accepted.tq: Match a reorganisation outcome with the movements that demanded it.

accepted.s: On which date did Bombay State become divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat?
accepted.x: Bombay State was divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of Bombay’s bifurcation from the later Punjab reorganisation date.

accepted.s: The Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 resulted in which of the following arrangements?
o: Punjab was divided into three States, with Chandigarh transferred to Delhi.
Punjab and Haryana were created; Chandigarh became a Union Territory and shared capital.
Haryana and Gujarat were created; Chandigarh became part of Maharashtra.
Punjab was merged with Himachal Pradesh; Chandigarh became the sole capital of Haryana.
accepted.x: The 1966 reorganisation divided Punjab into Punjab and Haryana, while Chandigarh was made a Union Territory and served as their shared capital.
accepted.tq: Test the complete institutional consequence rather than only the names of the new States.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1956 — Bombay divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat
1966 — Chandigarh made a Union Territory and shared capital
1966 — Punjab divided into Punjab and Haryana
1960 — Bombay divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat
accepted.x: Bombay was divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960, not 1956. The Punjab division and the status of Chandigarh belong to the 1966 reorganisation.
accepted.tq: Check the year against the specific reorganisation event.
